# `Q-12-22` — Listing Record Key Looks Misspelled

> A key in an inline `contents:` record is a near-miss of a listing
> field; it was kept as a custom field.

## What this means

An inline `contents:` record's curated keys (`title:`, `description:`,
`image:`, and so on) are typed into the item's built-in fields; every
other key is forwarded, verbatim, into `item.extra` for custom
templates to read. That forwarding is silent by design — custom
fields are a supported feature — so a typo'd curated key is otherwise
invisible: it doesn't error, it just quietly becomes a custom field
the built-in templates never look at.

This warning flags a key that is *close* to a known listing field
name, on the theory that it is more likely a typo than a deliberate
custom field.

## Why this happens

Common near-misses:

```yaml
listing:
  contents:
    - title: Get started
      descripton: Download and install    # meant `description:`
      Title: duplicate case-typo of title  # meant `title:`
```

The check compares each unrecognized key against the curated field
names using edit distance (insertions, deletions, substitutions, and
adjacent-character swaps each count as one edit): keys of 5 characters
or fewer must match within 1 edit, longer keys within 2. `name` is 2
edits from `date` and is *not* flagged — short, unrelated words don't
trigger it.

## How to fix

- If the key was meant to be a curated field, rename it:

  ```yaml
  listing:
    contents:
      - title: Get started
        description: Download and install
  ```

- If the key is intentional — a custom template reads `item.descripton`
  on purpose — no change is needed; the warning does not block
  rendering, and the key still reaches `item.extra` either way.
